problem_type: Generic name sanitizer truncates stored asset file names including the extension
symptom: Real paid run T4 (2026-09-26): an Agent-generated video landed in the project as a `.bin` file. Inside Nomi it plays (type is sniffed from bytes), but canvas Download saves `.bin`, Windows cannot open it by double-click, and MCP preview answers application/octet-stream.
direct_cause: electron/projects/repository.ts sanitizeName truncates the whole string to 90 characters. electron/assets/projectAssetStore.ts uniqueAssetPath and writeDeterministicAsset passed the full file name (stem + extension) through it, so a long provider URL basename (signature/hash segments, ~148 chars) lost its extension and both paths fell back to `.bin`. Separately, generationOutputMaterializer.fileNameFor took `path.basename(new URL(dataUrl).pathname)` for data: URLs, i.e. a slice of the base64 body.
class_root: Stored asset file names were cut by a sanitizer that knows nothing about extensions, and each write path decided the extension on its own (parse after truncation, fall back to `.bin`), so any caller handing in a long name silently lost the file type.
migration: Added storedAssetFileParts in projectAssetStore.ts as the single rule for on-disk asset names: extension from the byte-sniffed content type (canonicalAssetFileName), only the stem is sanitized and truncated to fit SANITIZED_NAME_MAX_LENGTH together with the extension. uniqueAssetPath (writeAsset, copyNativeFileToBucket, moveAssetFile) and writeDeterministicAsset now call it; their private `parse → || '.bin'` logic is deleted. data: URLs no longer yield a basename in fileNameFor.
affected_population: Every generation whose provider result URL has a basename longer than ~86 characters (Agent paid-card path, which keeps the provider file name)
Imports / copies / moves of local files with very long names

invariant_owner_layer.why: projectAssetStore is the only layer that writes asset files to disk; storedAssetFileParts is the one naming rule every write path uses, and its tests use the real sanitizeName (the previous tests mocked it as non-truncating, which is why this was never caught).

invariants: Every asset file written under assets/ ends with the extension of its byte-sniffed content type; the extension is never truncated
The stored name (stem + extension) fits SANITIZED_NAME_MAX_LENGTH; only the stem is shortened
A data: URL never contributes a file name
residual_risks: Content-addressed uploads (uploadContentStore.publish) keep the original basename untruncated; a pathologically long local file name could hit Windows MAX_PATH. Different failure (write error, not a wrong type) and not observed; left as is.
sanitizeName is still used for display names and project folder names, where truncation without an extension is correct; its doc comment now says not to use it for stored asset file names.
internal_only_reason: Purely internal naming logic; no external format or API is involved — the extension is derived from our own byte sniffing (canonicalAssetFileName).

recurrence.reason: Four write paths each re-derived the extension after a generic truncation; any new write path or any provider with long URLs reproduces it. It has existed since 2026-08-24 and only surfaced when the Agent path started keeping provider file names.
same_class_scan: electron/capabilityCore/generationOutputMaterializer.ts fileNameFor — data: URL no longer yields a basename
electron/assets/uploadContentStore.ts:43 publish — keeps the untruncated basename; extension preserved; not affected
electron/assets/projectCacheFile.ts:20 — names are `<bucket>-<8 hex><ext>`, far below the limit; not affected
electron/projects/repository.ts:80,203 — display name / project folder name, no extension semantics; not affected

generality_proof: All on-disk asset naming in projectAssetStore now goes through storedAssetFileParts, which takes the content type as input and budgets the stem after the extension, so no caller can hand in a name that loses its type; new write paths reuse uniqueAssetPath or writeDeterministicAsset and inherit the rule.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The single rule for stored asset file names: extension from sniffed content type, only the stem truncated

same_class_entry_points.evidence: writeAsset / copyAssetFile / moveAssetFile tests with 120-char names (with and without extension) end in .mp4 within budget; red on the old code (mutation run 2026-09-26)
Two writeDeterministicAsset tests end in .mp4; red on the old code; the long-name walk stores `seedance-output-…-<key>.mp4`
Two data: URL tests (base64 with and without a slash) name the output generation-output.<ext>; red on the old code
Uses path.basename(fileName) without sanitizeName truncation, so the extension is preserved

prevention.invariant: Stored asset names keep the sniffed extension and fit the name budget
prevention.failure_mode: projectAssetStore.test.ts long-name cases fail (they use the real sanitizeName); the long-name walk fails on the stored path or the download default name
prevention.strategy: One naming function takes the content type and budgets the stem after the extension; write paths no longer parse names themselves

legacy_paths.rationale: The per-path `path.parse(sanitizeName(...))` + `|| '.bin'` logic in uniqueAssetPath and writeDeterministicAsset is deleted in the same diff.
